data.claim: (1) pyyaml is NOT a ddflow dependency (pyproject lists only jinja2; the venv has no yaml module; adopt.py already edits YAML as text for the same reason), so the config must be parsed with a stdlib-only reader. (2) pre-commit 4.6.1: the generated hook carries '# File generated by pre-commit' and ARGS=(hook-impl --config=<path> --hook-type=<name>); a hook runs at stage S iff S is in its stages, which default to top-level default_stages, which default to ALL stages; legacy names commit/push/merge-commit map to pre-commit/pre-push/pre-merge-commit; an executable <name>.legacy in the hook dir is also run. (3) current enforce.installed only greps HOOK_MARKER, so run_nemo_run reports both hooks NOT installed, exit 2.
data.falsifier: yaml importable from ddflow's venv, or pre-commit's clientlib defaulting stages to something other than default_stages/STAGES, or hooks status on run_nemo_run printing installed.
data.probe: python -c 'import yaml' (ddflow venv); grep default_stages/STAGES/_STAGES pre_commit/clientlib.py + repository.py:123; read install_uninstall.py + hook_impl._run_legacy; ddflow --repo run_nemo_run hooks status
data.probe_output: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'; clientlib: STAGES=(*HOOK_TYPES,'manual'), StagesMigration('default_stages', STAGES), _STAGES={'commit':'pre-commit','merge-commit':'pre-merge-commit','push':'pre-push'}; repository.py:123 'if not ret[stages]: ret[stages]=root_config[default_stages]'; hook_impl: legacy_hook=<hook_dir>/<type>.legacy run if os.access X_OK; status: 'pre-commit hook: NOT installed ... commit-msg hook: NOT installed -- but ... NOTHING checks it' exit 2
data.question: How does a pre-commit-framework hook decide which configured hooks run at a stage, and can ddflow read .pre-commit-config.yaml with what it already depends on?

evidence.note: Research Rb5432fc845 CONFIRMED: 'import yaml' in ddflow venv -> ModuleNotFoundError (no YAML dep; pyproject lists only jinja2); pre-commit 4.6.1 clientlib/repository: hook stages default to default_stages, default ALL STAGES, legacy names commit/push/merge-commit mapped; hook_impl runs <type>.legacy if executable; 'ddflow --repo run_nemo_run hooks status' -> both NOT installed, exit 2.

YAML: stay stdlib-only per pyproject + adopt.py precedent. Recoverable items listed belong to other agents; not touched.

commit 6ac3ed6: enforce.armed()/Armed + stdlib-only reader for .pre-commit-config.yaml (read_precommit_yaml, UnreadableYaml) + precommit_hooks_running (stages->default_stages->all, old stage names, entry+args, language fail, check-msg pass_filenames:false, <hook>.legacy); installed() = bool(armed().via); _hooks_status says how armed and gives a config remedy over a framework hook. Regression test tests/test_hooks_status_precommit.py: 23 passed; with main's setup.py+enforce.py restored it fails: 'AssertionError: status exit 2 ... pre-commit hook: NOT installed'. Reader matches PyYAML on 26 real pre-commit configs/manifests + 37 synthetic cases (only differences: two invalid-YAML inputs PyYAML rejects). Related tests (15 files): 309 passed, 1 skipped. run_nemo_run status via worktree: both 'installed -- armed through the pre-commit framework', exit 0.

refute-prompted Sonnet subagent (independent, saw only diff+intent), probed with real pre-commit 4.6.1 and 20k mutation-fuzz configs vs PyYAML. CONFIRMED and fixed in 028375e, each with a fail-first test (8 tests fail on 6ac3ed6): (1) FALSE PASS: files/exclude/types filters ignored - pre-commit skips a filtered hook '(no files to check)' -> now armed only with no filters or always_run: true; (2) RecursionError escaped armed() on deep nesting -> UnreadableYaml; (3) ValueError (NUL in --config path) escaped -> 'could not read'; (4) 'echo hooks check-commit' counted -> command must name ddflow; (5) YAML 1.1 yes/on, multi-document accepted -> handled/refused. Held up: stage rules, default_stages, legacy names, no-ddflow framework hook NOT installed, non-exec hook, missing/binary config, pass_filenames:false, language: fail. Remedy wording note taken: dropped 'then pre-commit install'. Same family as the author; the cross-family check is the critic gate.

evidence.note: Manual sweep: duplicate top-level names in enforce.py -> one collision (_key, pre-existing trailer helper) found and my YAML helper renamed _yaml_key; repeated shlex-with-fallback in enforce.py factored into _words (c6fa136); grep across ddflow/ for pre-commit/YAML parsing, _as_list/_true/_false-style helpers, 'File generated by pre-commit' -> none elsewhere on main (the B-precommit-companion generator is unmerged and writes, not reads); status wording reuses one _hook_line/_hook_remedy, CHECK_COMMAND is the single printed spelling. roborev duplication analysis could NOT run: job 846 (kilo/LAN) sat queued/running ~2h on a saturated endpoint and was canceled; job 853 (claude-code agent in the daemon) 'failed after 3 retries: agent: claude-code failed'. So the roborev leg of this gate is unavailable; this pass rests on the manual sweep above.

data.summary: complete after merge warns that EVERY gate 'passed on a different tree' even when the tested tree is identical to what landed. completion.verdict takes wt = W.load_path(repo, it.worktree) or repo; merge (remove_on_merge) has already deleted the worktree, so tree_fingerprint runs on the PRIMARY checkout: HEAD is the merge commit (a different commit sha) plus other agents' dirty files. Seen on B-fix-hooks-status-precommit: unit_tests evidence c6fa13645a13+..., merge commit f998381 with 'git diff c6fa136 f998381' empty, yet complete printed the NOTE for unit_tests, standards, critic and rubber_duck. The driver's own order is merge -> complete, so the warning fires on the ordinary path and teaches agents to ignore it. Fix direction: fingerprint the merged branch tip (or compare git tree objects, not commit shas), or check staleness at merge time.

data.rule: When detecting another tool's hook (pre-commit framework), model its skip rules -- stages/default_stages, file filters without always_run, pass_filenames, language fail/pygrep, remote manifests -- and report anything unreadable or unverifiable as NOT installed with the reason; three reviewers each found a false 'installed' the first version missed.
data.title: A hook counts as armed only if the thing that runs it would run ddflow's check on every commit
